sound: he (e as the particle that marks where someone is going)
components: a short rise to a low peak
a longer run down to the right
strokeOrder: start low on the left and rise to the low peak
without lifting, turn over the peak and run down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03078 file records へ as a single stroke path in this order and direction: the rise from the left, the peak, then the longer run down to the right; so there are no pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03078.svg, hiragana へ (U+3078 HIRAGANA LETTER HE), one stroke path kvg:03078-s1 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores へ as one directed path in writing order: it starts low on the left, rises to a peak left of the middle, turns over it and runs down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.

notes: The he of へや, a room, and the last sign of the row は, ひ, ふ, へ, ほ. As the particle that marks where someone is going, it is read e, the way は is read wa as the topic marker.
